name: Federal Opportunity Zones
summary: Created by the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and made permanent by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, Pub. L. 119-21, July 2025) on a 10-year designation cycle. OZ 2.0 governor nominations underway July 2026; new OZ 2.0 map effective 1/1/2027. Existing OZ 1.0 tracts remain valid through 12/31/2028.

OZ 2.0 (effective 1/1/2027): 5-year rolling deferral, 10% basis step-up at 5 years (30% for rural QOFs)
Pre-2027 OZ 1.0 investments trigger deferred-gain inclusion on 12/31/2026 unless rolled into OZ 2.0
OZ 2.0 caps total exclusion at 30 years post-investment
howToApply: Invest capital gains into a Qualified Opportunity Fund (QOF) within 180 days
QOF must hold at least 90% of assets in OZ property
File IRS Form 8996 annually (expanded reporting beginning 2027)
Work with a tax advisor familiar with OZ 1.0 vs OZ 2.0 transition
requiredDocs: Property records within the Opportunity Zone
contact: IRS Opportunity Zone resources or local CDFI

Most industries qualify except sin businesses (golf, gambling, liquor stores)

name: Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF)

Can combine with other TIF incentives

Business financial statements (to determine reimbursement tier)
